details: This package is an unofficial fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that, without the operator's knowledge, uses the operator's authenticated WhatsApp session to join a third party's group and follow two third-party newsletter channels. lib/Socket/newsletter.js contains three module-level setTimeout(..., 90000) blocks inside makeNewsletterSocket; they run 90 seconds after any consumer creates a socket and: (1) call sock.groupAcceptInvite('E9AX0T7jKJ48VFAI4zuxC8'), joining the group behind hxxps://chat[.]whatsapp[.]com/E9AX0T7jKJ48VFAI4zuxC8; (2) and (3) issue a follow query (QueryIds.FOLLOW, xmlns "w:mex") against the base64-obfuscated newsletter JIDs MTIwMzYzMzg5MDEyMDk0ODU2QG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI= and MTIwMzYzNDIzODkwMDU0Nzg3QG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI=, i.e. 120363389012094856@newsletter and 120363423890054787@newsletter. Separately, lib/Socket/dugong.js hard-codes a forwarded-newsletter tag on outgoing forwarded messages pointing at 120363297591152843@newsletter under the display name "shenvn.". The 90-second delay and the base64 encoding of the channel identifiers hide the account actions from the operator; failures are swallowed in empty catch blocks. Errors are suppressed so the account changes happen silently. The preinstall hook (engine-requirements.js) only checks the Node.js major version and is unrelated. No npm/GitHub/cloud tokens, SSH/AWS credential files, environment variables or local files are read or transmitted; all traffic goes to WhatsApp infrastructure.
